name: GPU clouds & neoclouds
summary: Companies that own huge GPU clusters and rent slices of them by the hour, from big general clouds to specialist GPU-only providers.

D1.guide: Guess first: is it cheaper to rent a GPU for a year or buy one?
text: Most people building AI don't own the giant computers it runs on. They rent them, a bit like hiring a car instead of buying one.
Some rental companies sell every kind of computer service. Others, called neoclouds, mostly rent out powerful AI chips.
D1.analogy: Hiring a car instead of buying one.

text: **Hyperscalers** are the big general clouds: GPUs sit beside storage, databases, identity and networking you may already use, with many regions and compliance certifications.
**Neoclouds** are specialist GPU clouds. They focus on accelerators, often offer newer chips sooner or simpler pricing, and run fewer other services.

You can rent **on demand** (pay by the hour, may be unavailable), **reserve** capacity for a fixed period (cheaper per hour, you pay even when idle), or **own** hardware. Renting suits bursty or uncertain workloads; owning pays off only if the GPUs stay busy for years.
D2.analogy: Hiring a car by the day, leasing one, or buying one outright.
D2.analogyBreaks: Hire cars are interchangeable and plentiful. The newest GPUs are scarce, can sell out in a region, and large training jobs need thousands of them networked together in one place, which a rental counter can't promise.

predict.question: A team needs 64 GPUs for a two-week experiment and isn't sure it will need them again. What fits best?
options: Rent them for the two weeks
predict.explanation: Short, uncertain demand suits renting. Buying or long reservations only pay off when the hardware stays busy for a long time.

text: Where it gets harder: capacity for the newest chips often has to be reserved weeks or months ahead, so availability can matter more than price.
Specialist GPU clouds depend heavily on a few chip suppliers and large customers, and nobody yet knows how fast today's GPUs will lose their value as newer generations arrive.
